2c9d519db3:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cuius celébrat per orbem,
Hódie lætus méruit secréta
Scándere cæli.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit eius
Córporis artus.

Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis eius méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

thy bishops’ fadeless crown, draw near:

Today attained a glorious fame;
Whose yearly feast, in solemn state,
Thy faithful people celebrate.

<h>T</h>he world and all its boasted good,
As vain and passing, he eschewed;
And therefore with angelic bands,
In endless joy forever stands.

<h>G</h>rant then that we, most gracious God,
May follow in the steps he trod:
And, at his prayer, thy servants free
From stain of all iniquity.

All glory, praise, and thanks we bring:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.

Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,

Omne per ævum.

Trinus et unus.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>T</c>his the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph
Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness
Erst on this feast-day merited to enter
Into his glory.

<h>S</h>aintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,
Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.
While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,
Quickened his being.

<h>S</h>ick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,
Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,
Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,
At his petition.

<h>W</h>hence we in chorus gladly do him honour,
Chanting his praises with devout affection,
That in his merits we may have a portion,
Now and forever.

<h>H</h>is be the glory, power and salvation,
Who over all things reigneth in the highest,
Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,
Onely and Trinal.
Amen.

<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>I</c>ste Conféssor Dómini sacrátus,
Festa plebs cuius celébrat per orbem,
Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
Laudis honóres.

<h>Q</h>ui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
Sóbrius, castus fuit et quiétus,
Vita dum præsens vegetávit eius
Córporis artus.

<h>O</h>b sacrum cuius túmulum frequénter
Membra languéntum modo sanitáti,
Quólibet morbo fúerint graváta,
Restituúntur.

<h>U</h>nde nunc noster chorus in honórem
Ipsius, hymnum canit hunc libénter:
Ut piis eius méritis iuvémur
Omne per ævum.

<h>S</h>it salus illi, decus atque virtus,
Qui supra cæli résidens cacúmen,
Tótius mundi máchinam gubérnat
Trinus et unus.
Amen.

<c>V</c>ox clara ecce íntonat,

54be439041:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>C</c>elestial Word, to this our earth
Sent down from God's eternal clime,
To save mankind by mortal birth
Into a world of change and time;

<h>E</h>nlighten our hearts; vain hopes destroy;
And in thy love's consuming fire
Fill all the soul with heavenly joy,
And melt the dross of low desire.

<h>S</h>o when the Judge of quick and dead
Shall bid his awful summons come,
To whelm the guilty soul with dread,
And call the blessed to their home.

<h>S</h>aved from the whirling, black abyss,
Forevermore to us be given
To share the feast of saintly bliss,
And see the face of God in heaven.

<h>T</h>o God the Father and the Son
Our songs with one accord we raise;
And to the Holy Spirit, One
With them, be ever equal praise
Amen.

Their endless hope to Thee that bow;

How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,

Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.

<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Heb 1:1-2</r>
<c>M</c>ultifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>A</c> solis ortus cárdine
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

<h>B</h>eátus Auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

<h>C</h>astæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ báiulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

<h>D</h>omus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Verbo concépit Fílium.

<h>E</h>níxa est puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem matris alvo géstiens,
Clausus Ioánnes sénserat.

<h>F</h>œno iacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Parvóque lacte pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

<h>G</h>audet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

<h>G</h>lória tibi Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis.
ee3e0d0756:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Heb 1:1-2</r>
<c>G</c>od, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>F</c>rom lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

<h>B</h>lest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

<h>I</h>n that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

<h>T</h>he mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

<h>T</h>hat Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

<h>T</h>he manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

<h>T</h>he heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

<h>A</h>ll honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini.
<r>℟.</r> Deus Dóminus, et illúxit nobis.
